history.p: According to a letter from Gade to Hermann Härtel dated 13 June 1849, he had started composing the octet while he was still in Leipzig; however, he did not finish it until he was back in Copenhagen, where he had plenty of time to compose music because the musical activities were lying still due to the war with Germany.

physDesc.physMedium: Label on the front cover: "Mus. ms. 983 / 156 / Niels W. Gade / Op. 17. / OKTETT / 20" together with the stamp of the Breitkopf & Härtel archive, which is also to befound on p. 1. Written in ink. Paper: 20 staves. Paginated 1-57. The first movements are dated May 1848. At the end of the music: "Fine Copenhagen 29 Juni 1848" and Gade's musical signature.

In quarter binding with blue paper sides and yellow spine with a handwritten label in Gade's hand inscribed: "Octett / von / N.W. Gade / Op. 17 / Partitur." On the flyleaf inscribed: "Till / Ludvig Norman / af vännen / Ivar Hallström / Stokholm den 24 December 1855." Written in ink. Paper: 12 staves. Paginated 1-204. Heading on p. 1: "Octett / für / 4 Violinen, 2 Bratschen und 2 Violoncelle / componiert von / Niels W. Gade. / Opus 17.".
